1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide __wherein the non-native compartment is engineered to contain a heterologous enzyme not naturally present in the same bacterial species from which the BMC polypeptide is derived__.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 __further__ wherein the non-native compartment is self-assembled in vivo.

3. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one __heterologous__ targeted enzyme __not naturally associated with the BMC polypeptide in its native bacterial species__.

4. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 wherein the non-native compartment comprises a plurality of different targeted enzymes __from different metabolic pathways or different organisms__.

5. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 or claim 4 wherein the at least one targeted enzyme comprises a compartment-specific targeting signal sequence __that directs localization of the enzyme into the non-native compartment__.

6. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the BMC polypeptide comprises a Eut polypeptide __and at least one additional heterologous enzyme for ethanolamine metabolism__.

7. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 6 wherein the Eut polypeptide comprises a EutS polypeptide.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides __from at least two different bacterial microcompartment operons or species__.

9. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different bacterial species __and at least one heterologous enzyme not naturally present in any of those species__.

10. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different BMC operons __and the non-native compartment contains a heterologous enzyme from a third organism__.

11. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein at least one BMC polypeptide comprises an affinity tag __and at least one heterologous targeted enzyme__.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide __and at least one heterologous enzyme not naturally associated with that BMC polypeptide in its native bacterial species__, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and __the heterologous enzyme, and to produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one BMC polypeptide and the heterologous enzyme, wherein the heterologous enzyme catalyzes a metabolic conversion__.

13. (Original) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a bacterium.

14. (Original) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Enterobacteriaceae.

15. (Original) The method of claim 14 wherein the member of the family Enterobacteriaceae comprises E. coli.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Shewanellaceae __and the heterologous enzyme is from a different bacterial species__.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a yeast __and the BMC polypeptides and heterologous enzyme are from a bacterial source__.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17 wherein the yeast comprises a member of the family Saccharomycetaceae __and the heterologous enzyme catalyzes a non-native metabolic pathway in the yeast__.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 18 wherein the member of the family Saccharomycetaceae comprises Saccharomyces cerevisiae __and the heterologous enzyme is not naturally expressed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae__.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises an alga __and the BMC polypeptides and heterologous enzyme are from a bacterial source not naturally present in the alga__.

21. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, and at least one __heterologous__ enzyme that catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product __wherein the enzyme is not naturally associated with the BMC polypeptide in its native bacterial species__; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product __for the purpose of producing a desired metabolite or degrading a toxic substrate__.

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a bioactive product __not naturally produced by the host cell__.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a drug or a drug precursor __not naturally produced by the host cell__.

24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a biofuel or a precursor of biofuel production __not naturally produced by the host cell__.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the at least one enzyme catalyzes a step in degrading or detoxifying a toxic substrate __and the non-native compartment sequesters toxic intermediates__.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 further comprising isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments __that contain the heterologous enzyme__.

27. (Original) The method of claim 26 wherein at least a portion of the non-native compartment comprise an affinity tag and isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments comprises contacting a sample comprising the non-native compartments with an affinity substrate having selective affinity for the affinity tag.

28. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 comprising a plurality of compartments __each containing at least one heterologous enzyme__.
